stories.title: Davison Igbinosun: The draft day hate was way overblown
stories.summary:
A lot of folks on here were losing their minds when we drafted Davison Igbinosun, and honestly, the reaction was way overly critical.



	 



	I get where the frustration came from initially. If you watched him at Ohio State, the grabby play and the flags would drive fans batty. But look at the actual body of work—the guy put up great stats, and more importantly, his penalties dropped off dramatically in his final college season once he dialed in the technique.



	 



	Everything we’ve seen out of camp and preseason tells me this kid is a pure competitor. Is he going to get flagged sometimes as a rookie? Probably. Is he going to take some lumps adjusting to NFL receivers? Almost certainly. But what you are getting is pure nastiness, legitimate toughness, and a guy who flat out refuses to back down from anyone. He’s got the ideal physical traits and he’s ridiculously sticky in press-man.



	 



	I mentioned this in another thread, but his real value is going to show up on high-leverage downs. When we dial up a blitz on 3rd-and-medium and the DC needs corners who can get in a receiver's face, disrupt the timing, and hold up on an island for 2.2 seconds to let the rush get home, Igbinosun is built for that exact role.



	 



	Yeah, it's just preseason, but you can't teach that kind of edge. I really like what I'm seeing from him so far.

	By playoff season



	2022: 1 game — 5 carries, 13 yards

stories.title: Interesting comment from Leonhard's presser today
stories.summary:
I would recommend watching his entire presser if you get a chance. Leonhard is extremely bright and I get more excited about the potential for this defense every time I hear him talk. I'll be shocked if he isn't a head coach within three years.



	 



	This particular comment jumped out and feels instructive about where the defense is going:



	 



	



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			Jim Leonhard with some notable comments on Terrel Bernard:
		

		
			 
		

		
			“He’s so damn smart and sometimes you want him to turn his brain off and just go play free and react to what he sees rather than overthink it. That’s the biggest thing, it was a little more structured in what he was asked to do in the previous scheme. It was very much ‘I see this, I do this’. And just getting him to play a little bit more free was probably the number one thing. If you want to play the way we want up front, ahead of him, he’s gonna have to react a little bit more. And that was the number one thing he’s had to learn.”
		
	



	 



	It's interesting how Leonhard kind of takes a shot at the previous scheme. That wasn't his intention but it has to be said to get his point across.



	 



	For all the talk about the change to a 3-4, for me the biggest change is the change in mindset on defense and I think this comment speaks to it. With McDermott it was see the play unfold first, then react according to your strict set of rules. It was a play backwards not forwards kind of mindset that resulted in us giving up a lot of soft yards and frustrating 3rd down conversions. And every year we'd get to the playoffs and smart QBs and offensive coaches would know our rules and mercilessly take advantage of them.



	 



	Obviously every defense has keys and rules that the players have to follow but there is a middle ground between reckless and rigid. I think Leonhard has found the right balance and the results will show up in certain players looking better than they have before, the LBs being maybe the biggest beneficiaries of the change.



	 



	Ever since Brady took over the mantra of the coaching staff has changed from "do your 1/11" to "play free." It's an important distinction. Building a perfectly oiled machine is a nice idea, but great NFL defenses are made by players making plays. And Leonhard understands that his guys will be able to make more plays when they're playing on their toes instead of on their heels.

Andre Reed to get jersey retired by the Bills?(Not Confirmed)
stories.summary:
Apparently Jim Kelly let it slip during his annual golf tournament that he knows Andre Reed getting his jersey retired by the Bills is in in the works and could happen as early as next season.  The WGR guys also brought it up this morning.



	Link: https://www.audacy.com/wgr550/sports/bills/could-andre-reed-s-no-83-be-next-retired-by-bills



	 



	Thoughts Bills fans?



	 



	I will say I am surprised but I'm not against it.  I only say I'm surprised because they have already issued number 83 to other players over the years which is usually a sign the team doesn't have plans to retire the number.  But Reed is the best wide receiver in franchise history IMO and was the last member of that Core 4 from the Super Bowl years that hadn't gotten the honor so I don't have any issues with it although I think he was always looked at as a borderline player for that particular honor.  And to be honest I'm sure a big part of it on the Bills end is they want to be able to have a ceremony/enshrinement like that for the new stadium

stories.title: Former 1st round #12 pick Henry Ruggs: 3 to 10 yrs prison for drunk driving fatal crash
stories.summary:
https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/38162272/ex-raiders-wr-henry-ruggs-iii-sentenced-3-10-years-fatal-dui



	 



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			Ruggs, 24, had been under house arrest with alcohol and location electronic monitoring devices since pleading guilty in May to one count of DUI resulting in death and one count of misdemeanor vehicular manslaughter in the crash that killed Tina Tintor and her dog, Max. On Wednesday, Ruggs read from a statement directed at Tintor's family in which he apologized for his actions.
		

		
			"To the parents and family of Ms. Tintor, I sincerely apologize for the pain and suffering," Ruggs said.
		
	



	 



	Pretty sure Ms Tintor's family don't think 3 years is nearly enough punishment for burning her alive.
	
	Ruggs got what his attorneys asked for:



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			In court documents filed before the sentencing hearing, Ruggs' attorneys had asked the judge to keep the duration of their client's prison time to a range of three to 10 years. Chesnoff and Richard Schonfeld said Ruggs "wishes that he could turn back time and change the outcome of the tragic events of November 2, 2021."
		
	



	 



	I'm sure he does, what with being cut from the team and losing his career and all.  But he can't.
